Reducing feed-water flow or adding a metal-chelating additive directly addresses the root cause: chelator dose 60 restores titer to healthy levels (~63 g/L), while dose 80 shows slight efficacy loss (~61 g/L), likely due to chelator stress/toxicity. Dissolved-oxygen drift and temperature excursions were rigorously tested and ruled out as they had zero impact on titer despite being strongly suspected by operators. The optimal, sustainable fix is dosing the chelator at 60.
